title: Segmented plan shelves and ephemeral-environment metering PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for introducing segmented plan shelves and a first-class ephemeral-environment metering model. This ticket covers entitlements mapping, soft-overage windows, per-environment attribution (dev/stage/prod), burst credits for ephemeral environments, and billing reconciliation rules when ephemeral usage exceeds committed entitlements.
background: Customers have adopted ephemeral environments (preview apps, feature branches, ephemeral inference clusters) that consume tokens and concurrency but should not be billed the same way as long-running production workloads. Current billing aggregates usage at the project/customer level which makes it hard to offer discounted ephemeral credits, attribute costs by environment, or apply soft overage forgiveness for preview usage. Sales and CS teams have asked for a model that allows: (1) discounted burst credits for ephemeral environments, (2) clear attribution of usage to environment tags for invoice visibility, and (3) automated reconciliation and rollback for negative-balance situations caused by ephemeral spikes.
goals: 1) Add a plan-level concept of "shelves": named buckets (prod, non-prod, ephemeral) with configurable quota and overage behavior. 2) Implement ephemeral-environment default credit bundles applied at creation time. 3) Provide invoice-visible attribution by environment tag and an admin flow to reclassify usage. 4) Define acceptance criteria and edge-case reconciliation rules for overages and negative balances.
non_goals: 1) Price redesign for enterprise quotas outside the shelf model. 2) Real-time chargebacks to billing integrations (this will be in a follow-up). 3) Deep UX redesign of the console's billing pages (visual tweaks are ok).
requirements: R1: Plan shelves - product plans must include 0..N named shelves. Each shelf has quota_units (tokens), concurrency_units, and a shelf_type: {prod, staging, ephemeral}.
R2: Default ephemeral bundle - when an environment is created with tag 'ephemeral' the system auto-assigns a configurable ephemeral_bundle (e.g., 50k tokens/month + 10 concurrency-minutes).
R3: Attribution - every API call must include an 'env' attribute (dev|staging|prod|ephemeral). Usage records must persist the env tag and be queryable for invoices and dashboards.

R4: Soft overage window - ephemeral shelves should tolerate an overage grace window of 72 hours with no immediate invoice impact; usage beyond the window is billed with a configurable surcharge multiplier.

R5: Negative-balance reconciliation - if ephemeral usage temporarily pushes a seat/account negative, auto-retry billing within 48 hours, and if still unpaid, generate an alert to finance and optionally rollback ephemeral assignments to read-only until healed.
R6: Admin reclassification - finance/admin users can reclassify usage records from ephemeral->prod within 30 days with an audit trail and optional manual invoice adjustments.

R7: Rate-limiting interplay - when ephemeral shelf quota is exhausted, requests should fall back to global soft-throttle policy (throttle rate first, then reject) rather than immediately charging production overage rates.
R8: Reporting - billing export must include shelf, env, applied_bundle_id, and overage_flag for each usage row.
R9: Backwards compatibility - existing customers without shelves continue to be billed under the current aggregated model; we must provide a migration path and admin mapping UI.

R10: Edge case: deleted ephemeral env - if an ephemeral environment is deleted within the grace window, any associated ephemeral credits are forfeited but will not be billed as overage; if deleted after the grace window and overage occurred, normal billing applies.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Create plan shelves - A test plan with three shelves (prod, staging, ephemeral) can be created via the admin API and appears in the console with correct quotas.
AC2: Environment creation - Creating an environment tagged 'ephemeral' allocates the ephemeral_bundle and appears in the usage ledger with shelf=ephemeral for subsequent API calls.
AC3: Attribution test - Run a synthetic workload from 3 envs; billing export CSV shows correct shelf attribution and total aligns with token counters (within 0.5%).

AC4: Soft overage window behavior - For ephemeral shelf, if usage exceeds quota, verify no invoice line item is generated for 48 hours and no invoice amount appears until grace window ends; after 72 hours, billed overage matches multiplier config.

AC5: Fallback throttling - When ephemeral shelf quota is exhausted, requests are first soft-throttled (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) and only rejected after throttle policy thresholds; production shelf requests unaffected.

AC6: Negative-balance flow - Simulate forceful charge failure and confirm system retries for 48 hours, emits finance alert on final failure, and sets ephemeral environments to read-only if configured on the plan.
AC7: Reclassification - Admin reclassifies a set of ephemeral usage rows to prod; invoice preview updates and audit log contains username, timestamp, and original shelf.
AC8: Export completeness - Billing export contains shelf, env, bundle_id, and overage_flag fields for all usage rows in the test month and importable into accounting system without schema changes.

AC9: Migration path - For a selected existing customer, admin mapping UI successfully maps their current aggregated usage to newly created shelves producing an invoice consistent with prior billing +/- expected delta (<2% drift).
AC10: Documentation - Public PRD + Console help doc published; SDKs updated with new header 'X-Env-Tag' and example usage.
open_questions: Q1: Pricing delta - What surcharge multiplier should be recommended for ephemeral overage? Initial default proposed: 0.25x of prod unit price (i.e., cheaper).
Q2: Default bundle size - Should ephemeral default bundle be time-bound (monthly) or environment-lifetime-bound?
Q3: Deletion forgiveness - Under what conditions should we refund ephemeral tokens if an environment is deleted soon after provisioning?
Q4: International taxation - Does moving usage between shelves create tax implications when invoices change? Finance to advise.
Q5: UI complexity - How many shelves should customers be able to create before needing quota constraints?
implementation_notes: ENG will add shelf metadata to plan models, record 'env' attribute on usage events, and extend billing export schema. Billing job must incorporate grace-window state machine. Console will show shelf buckets on plan detail and allow admin reclassification. Security: ensure reclassification endpoint is RBAC-protected and writes to audit_log. Work to be split across ENG-21003 (usage pipeline), ENG-21200 (billing job), and ENG-21311 (console UI).
